subject: Film & Cinema
title: Screwball Comedy: Wit at Full Speed
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Screwball Comedy: Wit at Full Speed.

hook.text: In 1930s Hollywood, men and women argued at lightning speed — and audiences loved it.

buildup.text: Screwball comedies like Bringing Up Baby paired fast dialogue with absurd situations.

discovery.text: The Hays Code banned explicit romance, so attraction was expressed through verbal sparring.

twist.text: These comedies often featured strong, clever women who outsmarted their male leads.

climax.text: The screwball style influenced everything from sitcoms to romantic comedies.

punchline.text: The sexiest thing on screen was a good argument.

quiz.question: Why did screwball comedies use fast verbal sparring instead of romance?
options: The Hays Code restricted explicit romantic content
